main_body: A multi-storey campus/office block: a flat roof surface with rooftop units and a skylight on top, then a tall south facade with four floors of windows and a glass entrance
top_band: At x=64: a light parapet edge at rows 1-2 (L=226), then the roof surface at rows 7-37 (L=168/147, with tile seams), then a light front-edge line at rows 38-41 (L~190-235)
evidence: The roof is drawn as a large horizontal surface seen from above, with AC units and a skylight on it. It is closed at the front by a bright edge line (rows 38-41) and a green band, with a shadow row at row 42. Below that is a separate vertical facade with framed, inset windows and a recessed glass door. Both a top band and a front face are clearly present, and no receding side face is drawn. The roof is tall relative to the facade, but it reads as a flat roof, so this is acceptable as 3/4.

style.evidence: The grey-lavender ramps have about 5 steps: a white highlight, light, mid, dark and a deep outline. The dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline follows the material tone. The concrete speckle and the window glass diagonals add texture, and 5x5 flat-fill coverage is only 9%. The median of 9 colours per tile is close to the stone reference (11) but below house-h101 (18). The total of 32 colours is lower than both references (185 and 66). The repeated windows make it a little more uniform, but it would not look sticker-like next to the references.
